home.tagline: A sister-run neighborhood bakery in Santa Monica
body: Louma Bakery is rooted in European baking traditions with a Lebanese twist. We serve slow-fermented breads, classic pastries, seasonal offerings, and great coffee and matcha. From delicate viennoiserie and organic sourdough to nostalgic Lebanese classics such as our za’atar croissant and kaak bread.
Our small team bakes everything daily from scratch in our open kitchen on Wilshire Blvd. Each component of our menu is crafted with care and invites you into our story.
home.newsletterBody: The odd note about new bakes. Nothing else.

initiative.title: The Louma Initiative
intro: From the beginning, our vision has been clear: pair exceptional baking with real, life-changing opportunities. People with disabilities are deeply underrepresented in hospitality, an industry with so much room for growth, creativity, and community. We want to help change that.

We grew up hanging out in our family’s kitchen, and some of our closest moments as sisters happened there. So that’s where we started. Inspired by Louma’s own experience with intellectual and developmental differences, we set out to build a bakery where people of all abilities can learn, work, and feel valued. Everyone deserves the chance to build skills, gain confidence, and be part of a team that sees their talent.

sections.title: Opening doors
paragraphs: Our training and employment program is up and running. Our mission-based staff train alongside our team, learning skills they can take anywhere: food prep, packaging, customer service.

We partner with Breaking Barriers, an organization that specializes in supported employment. Their job coaches work one-on-one with our mission-based staff on site, so everyone has the support they need from day one. The goal is simple: real pathways into meaningful work, and more independence along the way.

sections.title: Built to last
paragraphs: Louma Bakery is owned by The Louma Initiative, a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit. The Initiative supports people with intellectual and developmental differences through four pillars: employment, research, education, and community outreach. The bakery is the employment pillar in action, and all of its profits go directly back to the Initiative. Every coffee and croissant helps fund the rest of that work.

menu.title: Menu
intro: We make everything in-house, from dough to filling, in our open-plan kitchen.
Our menu changes with the seasons, as we strive to use fresh ingredients as much as possible, however you’ll always find a few Louma classics on our counter.
Alongside the pastry case, you’ll find salads and sandwiches for lunch, granola to take home, and a full coffee, matcha, and tea bar.
We’re a small-batch bakery and sometimes the good stuff goes early. We recommend coming before 10 AM for the widest selection.
menu.allergenNote: Our kitchen handles wheat, dairy, eggs, nuts, and sesame. We can't guarantee any item is free of them. Ask us and we'll tell you what's in it.

careers.title: Work at Louma
careers.lede: We're hiring in the kitchen and at the counter.
body: Most roles don't need bakery experience. Showing up and wanting to learn counts for more.
We hire people who are often shut out of work, and train them to be great at it. Tell us a little about yourself and we'll be in touch.

roles.title: Training Track
roles.body: A paid, supported path into baking and counter work. Start here if you've never been given the chance. No experience needed.

roles.title: Baker
roles.body: Shape and bake bread and pastry through the morning. Experience helps; attitude counts more.

roles.title: Counter & Service
roles.body: Run the register and keep the case full and the room warm.

roles.title: Job Coach / Trainer
roles.body: Support and grow the Training Track team on the floor. Background in IDD support preferred.
